about: Feasibility of the Prague city-election programmes, 2026, within one four-year term: one row per promise: [promise, rating, why it can be done, why it cannot (or what limits it)]. rating: yes (the city decides it alone and can do it within the term) | likely (within the city's powers and the term, but dependent on something it does not fully control, such as a permit, a tender, hiring or the districts) | partly (the city can do a stated part within the term, such as preparation, a start or one of the grouped promises, but not the whole promise as worded) | no (the promise as worded is a finished result that cannot be reached within the term, and the row holds no smaller step of its own) | other (the decisive step for every part is a law or a decision of the state or another body). Rows were chosen by the author, without a fixed rule; related promises are grouped in one row and the rating is for the row as a whole. Text captured 29 September 2026 (the Praha Sobě PDF is dated 24 September 2026); rated 1 October 2026. Each row also lists the references (keys of 'refs'; PROG = the list's own programme) for why it can and why it cannot be done; a reason without a key rests on the author's reading of the programme and the city's practice.

lists.name: Praha Sobě
lists.verdict: Most of the programme can be done as 'we will start preparing', not as 'it will be finished'; the programme mostly words its large promises that way.
rows: Stop selling city flats and land
yes
The City Assembly decides on selling the property it manages itself, and it sets in the Statute which property the districts manage.

Flats and land entrusted to the districts are sold by the districts, so stopping all sales also needs a change to the Statute, which the City Assembly makes after discussing it with the district concerned; a later assembly can reverse either.
Relax parking minimums for new buildings
yes
Parking minimums are set in the Prague building regulations, which the city issues itself.
A change has to go through the regulation's adoption process, which takes months, not years.
PSP
Bring back the 'Prague package' for children's school meals and clubs; trees, wildlife care
yes
The city funds these from its own budget, and the sums are small against it.
A later assembly can cancel it.
Repair the Hlávka, Mánes and Čech bridges, with speed as a tender criterion
likely
The bridges are the city's, repairs are already being prepared, and the city has used speed as a tender criterion before.
Each repair still needs its permit and tender, so all three may not be finished in four years.
PROG
'Start preparing' 8 000 city flats
likely
Preparing projects on city land is the city's own work.
Preparation fits in the term, though 8 000 flats need land and design for every site; building them does not fit: the whole market completes about 6 000 a year, and the programme gives no timeframe.
P4
Take developer contributions as flats instead of money
partly
A developer can agree to hand over flats in a planning contract (an agreement in which a developer provides something to the city in connection with a building project).
The city cannot order it across the board; each contract is negotiated.
Set up an investment fund with cheap loans
partly
The city may set up a fund and borrow.
Setting the fund up, its rules and its first loans take much of a term.
More secondary-school places; buy places in private schools for 2027/28 meanwhile
partly
The city runs secondary schools as the region and can expand them.
New school buildings take longer than four years, and buying places in private schools was not checked against the law and has not been tried.
City ring road, stage 'Blanka II': start the geological survey
yes
A geological survey is a small, concrete step the city can order.
Only the survey is promised; the road itself is years away.
PROG
Ring metro line O, Hloubětín tunnel, Industrial half-ring (a planned road in the east of the city), new Holešovice bridge
no
The city can commission studies and design, but the programme promises the projects themselves, not their preparation.
Each is a decade-long project from preparation to opening, so none can be finished in one term.
'Finish building metro D'
no
The city can keep building.
No section is due to open within the term: the builder's plan gives 2032, after the term.
DPPD
100 % step-free crossings and public-transport stops
no
The city and its transport companies can rebuild stops and crossings every year.
Stops and crossings run across the whole city and the programme gives no count, so all of them in four years is out of reach.
The Prague motorway ring
other
The city can help with land and connections.
The motorway ring is planned and built by the state road agency.
PROG
Regulate Airbnb; raise the tourist fee
other
The city can enforce existing rules; it already charges the fee at the ceiling.

The city has no power to restrict short-term rentals under current law; the EU registration rules apply from 20 May 2026, and a Czech law to implement them was not checked. The fee cannot exceed the legal ceiling of 50 Kč a person a night.
OZV18
unverified: 'Prague has 175 billion crowns lying idle in its accounts': how much is committed to projects under way.
'We cut Prague's debt to a historic low.'
lists.overall: More concrete than usual, and it calls its large projects preparation. Its weak points are numbers without a timeframe (8 000 flats), absolute targets ('100 %', 'finish metro D') and a funding plan resting on an unchecked sum.

lists.name: Piráti
lists.verdict: Most can be done as preparation and administrative steps; the housing and transport numbers cannot be finished within one term.
rows: 'Prague will build several hundred flats every year' through its development company
partly
The city's development company can get permits and start building on city land.
The programme itself says most of the building comes in the next term.
PROG
An investment fund repaid from rents, 'no burden on the budget'
partly
The city may set up a fund and borrow from banks.
Whether rents will cover the repayments is unknown without costs and rent levels.
Long-term goal of at least 10 000 new flats a year
no
The city can plan and permit faster and build some flats itself.
About 6 000 flats are completed a year now, and the city does not build the market, so 10 000 a year is out of reach within four years; the programme calls it a long-term goal.
P4
PROG
Ask up to 30 % of flats from developers for 30 years, 30 % below market rent, in exchange for zoning changes
partly
The city can ask for flats in exchange for zoning changes through planning contracts.
Requiring 30 % from every developer was not checked against the Building Act and has not been tested; each contract is negotiated.
Multiple property tax on long-empty and wholly tourist buildings; short-term rental rules
partly

The city may raise the local coefficient on property tax, from 0.5 to 5, by area or group of property, or for specified, named properties by a general measure of the assembly, so it could raise the tax on buildings it names.

The law has no category for empty flats, so a tax defined by emptiness itself needs Parliament. The city has no power to restrict short-term rentals under current law; the EU registration rules apply from 20 May 2026, and a Czech law to implement them was not checked.
Minimum flat size 16 → 30 m²; lower parking minimums
partly
Parking requirements are in the Prague building regulations, which the city issues itself, so lower parking minimums can be done.

The 16 m² minimum was not found in the Prague building regulations, which set 8 m² for a habitable room; where it comes from, a city or a state rule, was not confirmed, so the flat-size part is not rated.
PSP
PROG
PSP
New districts (West City, New Kolovraty, East City) and an acceleration-zone act
partly
The city can run design competitions and plan the districts.
The acceleration-zone act is a state law the programme asks Parliament for, and building whole districts takes decades.
PROG
Finish tunnelling metro D, open the first section in 2032; prepare A, B, C extensions
partly
Tunnelling and preparing extensions are in the city's hands.
The first section opens in 2032 by the programme's own date and the builder's plan, after the term; extensions take a decade or more.
PIR
DPPD
Tram lines to Malešice, Jarov, Nové Dvory, Strahov; trams on Wenceslas Square
partly
The city builds tram lines through its transport company, and shorter lines fit within a term.
Each line needs its permit and land; how far each one is, the programme does not say.
Trams back on the Libeň bridge within two years; a new Vltava bridge
partly
The bridge is the city's, and the city decides on its repair.
The two-year deadline depends on the bridge's condition; a new bridge is years of preparation.
City ring road, Industrial half-ring with Hloubětín tunnel, Radlice radial
partly
The city can prepare the projects, as the programme says.
Tunnels and ring roads take a decade or more to build. A radial is a main road from the centre outwards to the ring roads.
PROG
Low-emission zone inside the city ring road
likely
The city council may set a low-emission zone by a general measure (a binding decision on a defined matter, neither an ordinance nor a decision on one person's case).

It takes effect at least 12 months after it is announced, so it has to be announced in the first half of the term; a charge to enter can be added by an ordinance of the City Assembly, at most 500 Kč a day multiplied by the inflation coefficient.
New secondary schools (Hradčanská, Barrandov, Písnická, Braník)
partly
The city runs secondary schools as the region and can build new ones.
Each building needs a permit and several years of work, so all of them by the end of the term is uncertain.
City rental agency from 75 to 500 flats
likely
The agency is funded and run by the city, so it can grow.
It depends on how many private landlords want to rent through it.
Take over the Na Františku hospital; raise the tourist fee
other
The city can negotiate with the hospital's founder and ask the state for a higher fee ceiling.
The hospital's founder is the Prague 1 district, which must agree; the fee's ceiling of 50 Kč a person a night is set by law.
NNFP
unverified: City flats are 'only 4 % of the housing stock'; the development company added '4 billion' in land value.
'At least ten thousand flats' used for tourists; an infrastructure backlog 'over 30 billion'.
That a fund repaid from rents will not burden the budget.
lists.overall: Concrete in places (lines, stations, schools, 75 → 500, 16 → 30 m²) and often gives its own timelines. The weakest parts are the housing numbers and promises that rest on state law; the two-year deadline for the Libeň bridge is uncertain.

lists.name: STAN
lists.verdict: Most can be done as preparation and starting construction; only the smaller items are promised finished, and several transport promises are not the city's to decide.
rows: Start building 2 000 city flats (Nové Dvory, Palmovka, Vršovice, Dolní Počernice, Jinonice)
likely
The flats are on city land, and the programme promises starts.
Each project needs a permit and a tender, and the programme does not say how far the five sites are prepared.
PROG
Long-term funding and management of city rental housing, with the European Investment Bank
likely
Funding and managing its flats is the city's budget and organisation.
The terms of a European Investment Bank loan are not in the city's hands.
Offer city flats first to young families, seniors and needed professions
yes
The city sets the rules for allocating its own flats.
Flats managed by the districts follow the districts' rules.
Complete metro D; a concept for line E
partly
Drawing up a concept for line E is within the city's reach.
Completing metro D is not possible in the term: the builder's plan gives 2032 for opening, and the whole line takes many more years.
DPPD
Tram lines to Nové Dvory, Strahov, Suchdol, Komořany 'and other parts'
partly
The city builds tram lines through its transport company.
Each needs a permit and land, so all of them in four years is out of reach.
Main station rebuild, metro S, rail link to the airport, the motorway ring
other
The city can plan with the state and argue for these projects.
Railways belong to the state railway agency and the motorway ring to the state road agency.
'We will start building the Vltava Philharmonic'
likely
The project and its money are the city's.
The start depends on a final permit and the contractor tender.
'We will start turning the Magistrála into a city avenue'
likely
The road is the city's and projects are prepared, so works can start.
Rebuilding the whole road takes longer than a term.
Recruit the 270 missing municipal police officers
partly
The city pays its municipal police and can raise pay and benefits.
Whether 270 people can be hired depends on the labour market.
More places in kindergartens, schools, children's centres and art schools
partly
The city runs secondary schools and can fund the districts.
Kindergartens and primary schools are run by the districts, so the city can add money, or build where a district agrees.
A new hospital in Letňany
other
The city can offer land and transport links.
The programme says itself that the hospital depends on the state and partners.
PROG
Short-term rental rules 'using new legal options'
other
The city can enforce what the law allows.

The city has no power to restrict short-term rentals under current law; the EU registration rules apply from 20 May 2026, and a Czech law to implement them was not checked. The row is rated on the law in force when checked; a Czech act implementing the EU rules could change it.
Shared bikes and scooters only at designated stands
likely
The city manages public space and can set where bikes and scooters stand.
How far it may fine operators is uncertain.
Stable funding for the city districts
likely
The city statute, which sets the districts' money, is changed by the City Assembly.
A change of the Statute has to be discussed with the districts, and part of their money comes from state tax sharing.
unverified: That exactly 270 municipal police officers are missing.
That the sites for 2 000 flats are 'ready' (permits, land).
Whether the EIB loan is agreed, and its size.
That the budget ends unspent because projects are late.
lists.overall: Concrete in places (sites, routes, the police number) and words large promises as starts. The weakest parts are transport promises held by the state, the city ring road and the hospital; costs and schedules are missing.

lists.name: SPD
lists.verdict: Fares, parking and the rules for city flats can be done; the ring road, radials and Airbnb rules cannot, because of construction time or because the city does not decide them.
rows: Finish the Prague motorway ring and the radials
partly
The radials are city roads, so the city can prepare and build them, and it can push the state on the ring.
The ring is planned and built by the state road agency, and the radials take a decade or more.
An annual public-transport pass for 1 000 Kč for residents
yes
The city orders public transport and may set the maximum fares in its transport plan.
The revenue lost has to be paid from the budget, and the programme does not say how much.
Greatly expand park-and-ride
partly
Car parks are on city land and paid by the city, so some can open.
A large increase needs new buildings, which take more than a term.
Underground car parks 'where possible'
partly
The city can choose sites, design and start the first builds.
Underground building in the city takes long to permit and build, so only a few could be finished.
Cheaper residents' parking, no further price rises
yes
Paid-parking zones are set in the city's own regulation, and the price follows the price rules; the city decides both.
A lower price is paid for from the budget, and a later council can raise it again.
A city-wide annual parking card for tradespeople
likely
The parking-zone rules are the city's.
The districts run parts of the system and have to agree.
One app for transport, parking and city services
likely
It is a city IT project.
Procurement and joining existing systems often delay such projects.
Repair empty city flats 'at once'
likely
The flats are city property and repairs are the city's decision.
Many flats are managed by the districts, which decide on those.
A new points system for city flats, priority for locals and some professions, end 'Housing First' (a flat first, with support, for homeless people) in its current form
likely
The city approves the rules for allocating its flats.
How far priority for locals can go before it is unlawful discrimination is uncertain.
Cooperative housing on city land, 'thousands of further flats'
partly
The city can choose land and a model for cooperatives.
Thousands of finished flats take longer than a term.
P4
Faster permits, high-rise building near the metro
partly
The city can change its building regulations and add staff.
The building act is the state's, and changing the zoning plan takes years.
PSP
Reasonable regulation of short-term rentals
other
The city can enforce existing rules.
The city has no power to restrict short-term rentals under current law; the EU registration rules apply from 20 May 2026, and a Czech law to implement them was not checked.
More money for crime prevention; supervised shelter for homeless people
likely
Crime prevention and the municipal police are in the city's budget.
New shelter sites may meet local opposition.
unverified: 'About 60 000 flats are missing.'
That money 'disappears in operating and inefficient spending', and how much could be saved.
That savings would pay for the ring road, radials, car parks and flats; the revenue lost to the 1 000 Kč pass.
lists.overall: The most concrete items (the tradespeople's card, the 1 000 Kč pass, the allocation rules) are within the city's powers. The weakest are the road projects and short-term rental rules; the housing plans lack numbers, dates and money.

lists.name: SPOLU
lists.verdict: Most of the programme can be done as preparation and as decisions within the city's powers; large builds, 10 000 flats a year and its demands on the state cannot be met within four years.
rows: Set conditions so that 10 000 new flats can be built every year
partly
The zoning plan, building regulations and city land are in the city's hands.
Completions follow years later; about 6 000 flats are completed a year now, and the building act is the state's.
PSP
P4
Metro D: start work on all sections from Písnice to Náměstí Míru in the following term
partly
The city can speed up preparation and permits.
Starting every section depends on permits, and the sections are at different stages of preparation.
DPPD
Speed up preparation of a ring metro line
likely
Preparing a new line is the city's work.
Building it takes a decade or more.
Complete the city ring road; a memorandum with the state
partly
The city can sign a memorandum on co-funding if the state agrees.
The money is the state's decision, and the road takes a decade or more.
Tender the Radlice radial; start preparing the Břevnov radial
likely
Preparing the tender is in the city's hands.
When building starts depends on the permit.
Start the Hloubětín tunnel; get a new Libeň bridge built
partly
The city is the builder, so it can start if permits and design are ready.
Completion takes longer than a term, and the programme does not say how far preparation is.
Push the state on the northern motorway ring
other
The city can press and cooperate.
The northern motorway ring is built by the state road agency.
Dynamic parking prices, visitor credits, a city-wide parking card
likely
Parking zones and prices are set by the city.
The districts have to agree, and the system needs changing.
A 'Pražanda' app for parking, transport pass, waste fee and discounts
likely
It is a city IT project.
Procurement and joining systems are the risk.
Raise the tourist fee to the European average
other
The city sets its own rate within the legal ceiling.
Prague already charges the ceiling of 50 Kč a person a night, so any rise needs Parliament to raise it.
OZV18
OZV18
Reasonable regulation of Airbnb
other
The city can enforce what the law allows.
The city has no power to restrict short-term rentals under current law; the EU registration rules apply from 20 May 2026, and a Czech law to implement them was not checked.
800 care-home places, 1 000 care workers, at least 150 respite places
partly
The city funds social services as the region and can expand home care.
New care homes take years to build, and staff are short.
Fiscal rules with a minimum level of investment
yes
The City Assembly sets its own budget rules.
A rule set by one assembly can be changed by the next.
Change the tax-sharing law, state co-funding, a pre-emption right, state land in Letňany
other
The city can negotiate.
Tax sharing needs Parliament, and so would a pre-emption right (a right of first refusal when land is sold; no statute was checked for it); co-funding and state land are the government's decision.
unverified: An Aa3 rating as 'the best possible' and among the best of European capitals.
District funding reform 'a billion a year extra'.
A heat plant 'for up to 200 000 people'; the Soutok park 'ten times larger than Stromovka'.
VAT on public transport 'further billions a year'.
lists.overall: Concrete mainly on named projects and on social-care numbers; much of transport is worded as preparation or as pressure on the state. The weakest parts are 10 000 flats a year and promises that depend on the state; for the projects it would start, the text does not show how far preparation is.

lists.name: ANO
lists.captured: 29 September 2026; the party's programme PDF returned HTTP 404 at capture
lists.verdict: Most promises can be done as preparation and management; the one number, 1 000 flats started a year, is uncertain within four years. The source is the lead candidate's page, not a full programme.
rows: Be starting 1 000 city flats a year by the end of the term
partly
The city can start building on its own land.
Reaching 1 000 starts a year by 2030 needs projects that are not yet prepared and permitted, and the text does not cost it.
P4
Repair empty city flats; clearer allocation
likely
The flats are city property and the city sets its allocation rules.
Many flats are managed by the districts.
One coordinator for road works, a public closure plan, speed as a tender criterion
yes
It is the city's own organisation and its tender conditions.
Speed as a tender criterion was not checked against the public procurement act, and a later council can drop the post.
Make completing the city ring road an investment priority
partly
The city decides its investment priorities.
Finishing the road takes a decade or more.
The motorway ring: 'an active partner of the state'
other
The city can cooperate on land and links.
The motorway ring is built by the state road agency.
Continue building metro D
partly
The city builds metro D and can continue.
The builder's plan gives 2032 for opening, after the term.
DPPD
Car parks and decks on housing estates; more park-and-ride
partly
The city can build on its land on the estates.
Each building needs preparation and a permit, and the text gives no scale.
More municipal police, a beat officer in every neighbourhood, security on night transport
likely
The municipal police and night-transport security are the city's.
Hiring depends on the labour market.
A city-wide programme to renew housing estates
likely
The city can start the programme and set a cleaning standard.
Upkeep is partly the districts', so results depend on them.
Develop the IKEM, Thomayer, Motol and Bulovka hospitals
other
The city can offer land and transport links.
All four are run by the Ministry of Health: Motol, Thomayer and Bulovka as university hospitals, IKEM as a state contributory organisation.
IKEM
unverified: 'Prague has able people, property and money': not quantified.
How many city flats stand empty.
The cost and funding of 1 000 flats a year.
Whether parking-zone revenue goes back into parking today.
lists.overall: Mostly qualitative, without costs or dates. The weakest parts are the large transport promises and the items that depend on the state. The rating covers the 6 priorities captured of the 10 the page announces.
